questions.question: A query suddenly runs far slower after a bulk load with no code change. What is the first fix the lesson suggests?
options: Add an optimizer hint to every query
Run ANALYZE TABLE and check the statistics
Switch to a different storage engine
questions.explanation: A plan flip often comes from an unlucky statistics sample; ANALYZE TABLE re-samples cheaply without rebuilding.

questions.question: When is a histogram most useful?
options: To speed up a single-table scan on one column
To give better estimates for low-cardinality unindexed columns, especially in joins
questions.explanation: Histograms improve estimates and so join order; they do not make scans faster, and an index is still the fix for single-column filters.

questions.question: How are histograms kept up to date?
options: They are not updated automatically; rebuild them yourself
Every time ANALYZE TABLE runs without options
questions.explanation: The lesson states histograms are not updated automatically and must be rebuilt on a schedule or after big loads.

questions.question: What happens if an optimizer hint is invalid?
options: The statement fails with an error
The hint is ignored with a warning, so check SHOW WARNINGS
questions.explanation: Invalid hints do not raise errors; they produce a warning only.
